Findings

1. **The scenes, line 173 (against the new cause in line 167).** Line 167 now starts the neat way by itself at the end of the crossing, while line 173 still says that after the crossing nothing else starts by itself. In line 173 replace the sentence `Nothing else starts by itself.` with:
`Where the crossing causes the neat way, that scene is the last part of this ending and gives way to any touch; after it, and everywhere else, nothing starts by itself.`

2. **The scenes, line 167.** Two faults in the pasted cause: "the second failed run" misses a child whose second failure is of another kind (runs three to eight can then fail on exactly what the idea answers, the cycle is judged badly, and nothing was shown, so "every idea gets its one showing" is false); and the crossing trigger now fires on positions whose one new thing is a vehicle, the barge, the thin kit, the longest gap or the free yard, for which the scene has no model of a way that fails and a way that holds (pack: game-design, guided-discovery.md). Replace the line with:
`- **The neat way** (shown once for each idea; 6 to 9 seconds). An idea is a part, a shape or a way of standing that a position brings as its one new thing: the plank on edge, the prop, the triangle, the row of triangles, the tube, the thread, the mast on a wide base and the arch. A position whose one new thing is a vehicle, the barge, the thin kit, the longest gap or the free yard has no neat way. Cause, on a sheet whose idea has not been shown: the first failed run of the job vehicle, from its second on, whose failure is one that idea answers; or, if the job vehicle crosses before any such run, the end of the crossing on that sheet, once the vehicle has parked. Either way the child has tried their own way first. An idea that a cycle ends without showing is still owed the next time its position is laid out. Beats: the chief pins a hand-sized model together in the margin from offcuts, first the way that fails (a square that leans over), then the idea (the same square with one diagonal); it stands on the model, which holds; it looks at the model, never at the child. Filled in from: the sheet's idea and, after a failed run, the kind of failure. From then on the model stands in the margin of every sheet of that position (rebuilt from `shown` and the sheet's position id) and can be pressed and plucked. It is never a model of the gap on the sheet.`

3. **The scenes, line 168.** The cause is "differ in more than one part", but the fill-in needs exactly two kinds of part: on a sheet whose kit is planks only (`plank-gap`, where line 219 says the trolley and the tracing are already open) every difference is of one kind, and elsewhere there can be three or more, so the chief's two models cannot be filled in. Replace the sentence `Filled in from: the two kinds of part in which the child's bridge and tracing differ, which are the two things the chief's models differ in; the models are never the child's bridge.` with:
`Filled in from: two of the differences between the child's bridge and the tracing, the two nearest the trolley, each a part added, left out, moved, turned or changed for another kind; those are the two things the chief's models differ in, and the models are never the child's bridge.`

4. **The designed order, and what is stored: lines 116 and 129 (ruling 5).** `waiting` now speaks for the newest sheet only, so a job vehicle sent home on a sheet taken back from the rack (line 173: a touch on the parked vehicle sends it home) has no stored place: line 116 puts it back on the far bank on load, which is round 1's finding 7 again for an older sheet.
Line 116, replace the sentence `It shows its job vehicle parked on the far bank if that vehicle has crossed the bridge as it stands, and at the near bank otherwise, both rebuilt from that sheet's own entry.` with:
`It shows its job vehicle parked on the far bank if that vehicle has crossed the bridge as it stands and has not been sent home since, and at the near bank otherwise, both rebuilt from that sheet's own entry.`
Line 129, replace `which vehicles have crossed it as it stands,` with:
`which vehicles have crossed it as it stands and whether its job vehicle has been sent home since,`

5. **The representation, line 58 (the builder's own change, not a paste).** "Only when posts tie it to the deck above" says more than the model: line 61 lets the calculation alone decide whether a build folds, and other parts (a diagonal to a footing, a second row of sticks making triangles) hold a hinged curve as well, so the sentence states as science a rule the game's model does not have (pack: game-design, ages-9-to-12.md; representation-before-game.md). Replace the line with:
`- Sticks pinned in a curve between two footings carry a load by squeeze and push outward on the banks: the arch. Its pins are hinges too, so a curve of three or more sticks does not keep its shape by itself: it holds only where other parts hold its joints, and the model works out whether they do.`
